auditor_premise_ACCEPTED: daily_card.py drives all games from ONE global np.random.default_rng(722); numpy's gamma/poisson are rejection samplers whose draw counts depend on parameters, so a form change re-couples the downstream stream. Bit-for-bit regeneration proves deterministic REPLAY, not a noise-free estimate. The observed 0.4545pp was therefore an unseparated sum of effect + coupling noise. This was correct and my earlier framing did not distinguish the two.

method.transcription_verified: harness/rng_noise_study.py --verify-math reproduces ALL 11 registered v3 probabilities EXACTLY under the frozen global-sequential RNG. Two transcription bugs were caught by that gate before any result was believed: (1) sim()'s trailing rng.poisson(1.0,n) was omitted — it does not enter p_home but it CONSUMES RNG and desynchronises every later game; (2) the card's ROUNDED park factor was used instead of the raw one. A third bug — a reduced ABBR map that split franchises carrying legacy full-name rows in results.csv into two teams — was also caught this way.
method.design: per-game keyed seeds (sha256 of game|rep), both arms under the SAME seed per replicate. This also REMOVES the slate-order confound that made v1-vs-v2 non-causal at the card level, because each game now gets its own independent stream rather than a position-dependent one.
method.study_A: n=30000 (frozen setting), 200 paired seeds — the distribution the single card is one draw from
method.study_B: n=2,000,000, 10 paired seeds — MC error ~0.035pp/run, so this estimates the TRUE parameter effect

RESULT_form_effect_is_REAL.games_distinguishable_from_zero: 11 of 11, at n=2,000,000, with CIs excluding zero
RESULT_form_effect_is_REAL.conclusion: the form effect SURVIVES noise separation. The near-noiseless estimate (0.4266pp) sits within 0.03pp of the single card's 0.4545pp, and per-game signed effects are stable between the two studies (e.g. CWS@CHC -0.682 vs -0.701; LAD@COL +0.621 vs +0.630). So the observed card delta was a good estimate — but that is now DEMONSTRATED rather than assumed.

RETRACTION_the_BAL_TB_flip.finding: the flip is NOT caused by form. The true effect moves BAL@TB from .508 to ~.5022 — still home-favoured. The card crossed .500 only because that single draw realised -1.2pp (true -0.58 plus ~-0.62 of coupling noise). The CI does not span .500 either. The auditor's specific challenge on this flip is UPHELD and my earlier '1 side flip' framing is RETRACTED: at 11 games, zero side flips are attributable to form.
RETRACTION_the_BAL_TB_flip.generalisation: side flips on near-.500 games are the least robust statistic on any card and should never be reported without a noise separation.
